written.q: Explain how the UniMart narrative becomes a data model and list five constraints you would enforce.
written.a: Each case statement yields entities: registration/login gives User (unique university email, password hash); listings give Listing, Category and ListingImage; messaging gives Conversation and Message; payments and orders give Order and Payment (unique provider reference and idempotency key); reviews give Review (one per completed order); notifications give Notification. Constraints: UNIQUE university_email; price >= 0 with DECIMAL; UNIQUE review order_id; rating 1 to 5; unique buyer/seller/listing conversation; legal order status transitions; version column for optimistic locking.

written.q: Describe the responsibilities of the controller, service, repository, entity and DTO layers in the Spring Boot backend.
written.a: Controller: parse path/query/body, trigger validation, call the service and map HTTP status; no repository calls or transactions. Service: business rules, ownership checks, transactions, orchestration. Repository: query and persist entities. Entity: persistence state and simple invariants, never returned directly. DTO/mapper: the API contract, preventing leakage of fields such as passwordHash.

written.q: Explain the environment-variable and secrets strategy and the role of Flyway and ddl-auto validate.
written.a: DB_URL, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET, JWT_ACCESS_MINUTES, APP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and the profile are supplied as environment variables; .env.example with placeholders is committed while .env and key files are ignored; production secrets come from the server environment or secret stores. Flyway creates and evolves the schema through immutable versioned migrations and Hibernate with ddl-auto validate only checks that entity mappings match it.

written.q: Trace one request end to end in the integrated app and list the required negative API tests.
written.a: A component calls an RTK Query hook; fetchBaseQuery adds the bearer token from Redux; the browser calls Spring Boot; Spring Security validates the JWT; Controller, Service, Repository and MySQL execute; a DTO returns as JSON; RTK Query caches it and React re-renders; mutations invalidate tags to refetch. Negative tests: no token 401, blank title 400, other seller's listing 403, missing listing 404, unfinished order review 409, another buyer's order 403, duplicate review 409, rating outside 1-5 400, expired JWT 401.

written.q: Describe the deployment architecture and CI/CD pipeline and explain why it is still a monolith.
written.a: One DigitalOcean Droplet runs Docker Compose with a MySQL container (persistent volume, healthcheck), a Spring Boot backend container and a frontend Nginx container, all behind a host Nginx reverse proxy (/api to the backend, / to the frontend) with TLS. GitHub Actions tests and builds on pull requests; on pushes to main it publishes images to GHCR and deploys over SSH with docker compose pull and up. It is still a monolith because there is a single backend deployable using one shared database; containers only package it.
